title: VS Code routes non-direct calls through the retired vertex tool name
status: confirmed within the explicitly recorded execution seam
component: UI extension, VS Code host and shared UI contracts
expected: Resolve and invoke the registered compact router (or the supported native tool) using the configured namespace.
actual: The actual activation entrypoint with an injected transport registered a working direct overview control. A memory_save request tried delendai_vertex four times and failed Tool delendai_vertex not found. The actual core registration function recorded only delendai_compact_router.
rootCause: The resilient proxy hardcodes vertex and reroutes every namespaced suffix outside a six-name allowlist before trying a native call.
impact: Most namespaced extension actions fail against the current core compact surface; direct overview/search controls can still succeed.
recommendation: Use the canonical discovery/resolution seam for compact routing and exact domain/action mappings; do not infer registration from visibility or legacy branding.

verification.result: exit0; actual activate/deactivate plus actual core registration; fake owned MCP transport and VS Code ports

relationship: New live extension routing cause. Prior G5#1 distinguishes historical residual brand names from live behavior; this is an exact operational retired name, not a generic rename census. G94#1/D36#1 concern payload accounting, not router identity. Existing discovery/broker behavior means hidden tools are not assumed unregistered.
limits: No real VS Code process, server child, provider or workspace. Memory request is captured by a fake transport and writes nothing. The registered tool name comes from the real registration function; no success of a real native server action is claimed.
regressionTest: Activation with core registration catalog: direct overview succeeds and non-direct memory request reaches compact_router exactly once, preserves args and configured namespace.
auditorOpinion: Fix at the host adapter contract. Do not add legacy aliases to the agnostic core just to preserve this hardcoded host assumption.

title: Dashboard theme and language controls submit stale form preferences
status: confirmed within the explicitly recorded execution seam
component: UI extension, VS Code host and shared UI contracts
expected: A theme or language chosen in the header/card controls is included in the saved settings payload.
actual: Actual compiled renderer in headless Chrome changes the root theme to light and language to es, while both outgoing settings saves still contain theme=system and language=en.
rootCause: Multiple control copies have no single synchronized settings state. Saving reads FormData from the settings form; applyTheme changes only the root. applyLanguage selects the first language select (header) and updates the header again, leaving the form unchanged.
impact: Header and theme/language-card changes can appear applied but save the previous values and revert on a host acknowledgement or reload.
recommendation: Maintain one settings draft, synchronize every mirrored control, and submit the chosen values; apply acknowledgements by request/revision.

verification.result: exit0; native Chromium events, actual compiled SCSS and actual generated dashboard script

relationship: New mirrored-control synchronization cause. UI-CFG01 is acknowledgement/edit ownership; UI-CFG02 is configuration discard baseline; prior G134#1 is web locale/base URL composition. These paths have distinct roots and regressions.
limits: Host API is an in-page capture port. Persisting real user settings was intentionally not attempted; stale outbound payload itself is proven. Browser stderr contains routine DBus noise and is preserved.
regressionTest: Change header/card theme and language; assert outgoing chosen values, form synchronization and acknowledgement/reload consistency in a real DOM.
auditorOpinion: A native DOM interaction test is required: string rendering and mocked element tests do not check duplicate-control ordering.

title: The first Start realtime click sends a stop command
status: confirmed within the explicitly recorded execution seam
component: UI extension, VS Code host and shared UI contracts
expected: The initial Start realtime control starts streaming.
actual: Headless Chrome clicks the initial control once and captures {command:logs,action:stop}; its label becomes Resume realtime.
rootCause: logsState.paused starts false while the rendered initial label/status is Start realtime/Realtime paused; the handler inverts it before choosing the command.
impact: The first attempt to start logs does nothing and contradicts the visible control. A second click can start it.
recommendation: Initialize paused=true or explicitly autostart and render the matching state; derive labels and commands from one state.
relationship: New initial toggle state defect, independent of view cleanup UI-LOG02 and the web SSE bootstrap D27#1.
limits: No real log backend was invoked. This proves the UI command contract emitted on the first click.
regressionTest: Assert first click start, second click stop, and matching labels after each change.
auditorOpinion: Small user-visible defect; group with dashboard control consistency work rather than a broad runtime redesign.

title: Disposing a dashboard view leaves its log polling loop running
status: confirmed within the explicitly recorded execution seam
component: UI extension, VS Code host and shared UI contracts
expected: Closing/disposal of a view aborts the subscription it owns.
actual: The actual provider plus actual LogsService using a fake client makes one subscribe request before disposal and a second subscribe request after disposal. The fixture sends an explicit stop to clean up afterward.
rootCause: onDidDispose clears only this.view; it never aborts logsAbort. subscribe limits yielded events rather than poll iterations, so an empty stream has no automatic iteration bound.
impact: Closed dashboards continue unnecessary MCP polling every 1500ms; repeated starts/hosts can retain work until explicit stop or process teardown. No provider cost or process-wide leak magnitude is claimed.
recommendation: Abort and clear the controller on view disposal and provider teardown; ensure panel-based dashboards have the equivalent ownership cleanup.

verification.result: exit0; beforeDispose=1 afterDispose=2 extraPolls=1; explicit stop cleanup; stderr empty

relationship: Qualifies prior G17#1: ordinary extension deactivate/client cleanup remains correct, but per-view disposal does not own its log controller. Distinct concrete ownership defect from the historical partial-activation concern. D27#1 concerns the web SSE bootstrap, not this VS Code polling loop.
limits: Only the sidebar provider is dynamically reproduced. Fake client returns empty owned log batches, with dashboard calls deliberately unavailable. No real VS Code or provider used.
regressionTest: Resolve view, start stream, dispose, advance past one poll interval and assert no further calls; assert teardown cancels pending waits and a replacement view owns its own controller.
auditorOpinion: Resource lifetime belongs to the host/view, not a max-events heuristic. Client abort-listener removal is already correct and is positive counterevidence against blaming the client wait helper.

title: The strict translation gate checks English-fallback dictionaries and misses 180 absent keys in ten locales
status: confirmed within the explicitly recorded execution seam
component: UI extension, VS Code host and shared UI contracts
expected: Strict completeness checks inspect raw per-language extension keys before fallback.
actual: All ten non-English/non-Spanish raw locales have61 extension keys versus241 English keys (180 missing each). The real --strict gate exits0 and prints 12 languages ×241 keys complete.
rootCause: withExtensionFallback inserts English keys before dictsByLang is exported, and the completeness gate consumes that already-filled runtime map. Type assertions also suppress raw contract omissions.
impact: The advertised strict parity gate cannot catch missing translations; most newer dashboard/preferences/logs text silently remains English in ten supported locales.
recommendation: Expose raw dictionaries for validation or validate raw imports before applying runtime fallback. Keep fallback for runtime resilience and report translation coverage separately.

verification.result: raw missing180 ×10; resolved241 ×12; actual gate exit0

relationship: Refines prior G8#1 with a newly reproduced concrete strict-gate cause: raw extension dictionaries are incomplete but the gate checks merged fallback values. D11#1 concerns separate web satellite namespaces; D72#1 concerns plugin extraction of used keys. G61-I18N-01 concerns corrupt plugin catalog behavior. Treat as a causal extension of G8, not an additional count of missing UI translations.
limits: No claim that every identical English value is a missing translation; finding counts only physically absent keys. Runtime English fallback is intentional and preserves rendering availability.
regressionTest: Delete one non-English raw key and require strict gate failure; verify runtime fallback still returns the canonical English value.
auditorOpinion: Keep fallback and make the quality gate honest. Do not break runtime availability to enforce translation completeness.
